summary:
With prefix sums `P`, the run `i..j−1` gains `P[j] − P[i]`. For each end `j`, keep candidate starts in a deque
with increasing `P`: a start with a larger `P` than a later one is never useful. While the front start reaches
the target, record the length and drop it (a later end would only be longer). O(n).

question.md:
Find the shortest run of consecutive days whose changes sum to at least `target`, or −1 if none exists.

- **Changes can be negative**, so a longer run isn't always better and the usual two-pointer window doesn't
  work: shrinking the window can increase its sum.
- **`target ≥ 1`**, so an empty run never counts.
- **Up to 10⁵ days; sums reach 10¹⁰**, beyond 32-bit integers.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- Negative changes: a sliding window doesn't work (shrinking can increase the sum).
- No run reaches the target: −1.
- A single day may already reach the target.

think.md:
**Prefix sums.** With `P[j]` = sum of the first `j` changes, a run from day `i` to day `j − 1` gains `P[j] − P[i]`.
We want the smallest `j − i` with `P[j] − P[i] ≥ target`. For `[4, -6, 3, 2, -1, 4, 1]`: `P = [0, 4, -2, 1, 3, 2, 6, 7]`.

**Two observations about candidate starts `i`:**

1. If a later index `j'` has `P[j'] ≤ P[i]`, start `i` is useless from then on: `j'` is a later start (shorter
   runs) with a smaller prefix (more gain). So keep starts with **increasing** prefix sums (pop the back).
2. Once start `i` has found an end `j` that works, any later end would only make a longer run from `i`. So pop it
   from the **front** after recording.

Together this is a monotonic deque over prefix-sum indices.

approaches.title: Every start, extended until it works

idea.md: From every start, extend until the sum reaches the target; the first time it does is the shortest run from that start.

build: Record the first length that reaches the target.

lines.text: Runs starting on day `i`; the sum is 64-bit in the typed languages.
The first end that reaches the target is the shortest from this start; longer ones can't beat it.

steps.text: Start day 0: the sum first reaches 6 at day 5 (sum 6), length 6.
Start day 1: never reaches 6.
Start day 2: the sum first reaches 6 at day 5 (sum 8), length 4.
Start day 3: the sum first reaches 6 at day 6 (sum 6), length 4.
Start day 4: never reaches 6.
Start day 5: never reaches 6.
Start day 6: never reaches 6.
Shortest: 4.

walk.title: Try every start day; extend day by day with a running sum, stopping at the first end that reaches the target.

limits.md: With negative values it can't stop early in general, so it scans everything. Prefix sums with the right data structure avoid that.

approaches.title: Prefix sums, increasing stack, binary search

idea.md:
Prefix sums, and an increasing stack of start indices (by prefix value). For each end `j`, binary-search the
stack for the **latest** start with `P[i] ≤ P[j] − target`, then push `j` after popping starts with larger or
equal prefix.

build: Binary-search the latest valid start for each end.

lines.text: `P[j]` = total change of the first `j` days; run `i..j−1` gains `P[j] − P[i]`.
Candidate starts and the best length (`n + 1` = none yet).
Each prefix index is an end, and afterwards a candidate start.
`P` increases along the stack, so the valid starts (`P ≤ P[j] − target`) form a prefix of it. Binary-search for its last element: the latest valid start, giving the shortest run ending at `j`.
Earlier starts with `P ≥ P[j]` are dominated by `j` (later and no larger), so remove them; then `j` becomes a candidate.

steps.text: End j = 0 (P = 0). No start has P ≤ -6. Push 0.
End j = 1 (P = 4). No start has P ≤ -2. Push 1.
End j = 2 (P = -2). No start has P ≤ -8. Then [1, 0] leave the stack (P no smaller and earlier than j). Push 2.
End j = 3 (P = 1). No start has P ≤ -5. Push 3.
End j = 4 (P = 3). No start has P ≤ -3. Push 4.
End j = 5 (P = 2). No start has P ≤ -4. Then [4] leave the stack (P no smaller and earlier than j). Push 5.
End j = 6 (P = 6). Latest start with P ≤ 0: index 2, length 4. Push 6.
End j = 7 (P = 7). Latest start with P ≤ 1: index 3, length 4. Push 7.
Shortest: 4.

walk.title: With prefix sums P, a run i..j−1 sums to P[j] − P[i]. For each end j we want the latest start i with P[i] ≤ P[j] − target. Keep candidate starts on a stack with increasing P and binary-search it.

limits.md: A binary search per end. Observation 2 shows a start can be discarded once used, which makes every step O(1) amortised.

approaches.title: Prefix sums with a monotonic deque

idea.md:
Monotonic deque of prefix indices with increasing `P`. For each `j`: while the front start gives a gain of at
least `target`, record `j − front` and pop it; then pop back starts with `P ≥ P[j]`; push `j`.

lines.text: Candidate starts in increasing `P` order, and the best length.
Each prefix index as an end.

The front has the smallest `P`, so if any start works for `j`, the front does. Record the length and drop it: any later end would make a longer run from it. Keep going, since the next start is later and may still work.
Starts with `P ≥ P[j]` are dominated by `j`: it's later and gains at least as much for any future end. Remove them, then add `j`.
The best length, or −1 if no run reached the target.

steps.text: End j = 0 (P = 0). Push 0.
End j = 1 (P = 4). Push 1.
End j = 2 (P = -2). Back [1, 0] have P ≥ -2: drop them. Push 2.
End j = 3 (P = 1). Push 3.
End j = 4 (P = 3). Push 4.
End j = 5 (P = 2). Back [4] have P ≥ 2: drop them. Push 5.
End j = 6 (P = 6). Front start(s) [2] reach the target: lengths [4]; drop them. Push 6.
End j = 7 (P = 7). Front start(s) [3] reach the target: lengths [4]; drop them. Push 7.
Shortest: 4.

walk.title: Same candidates, kept in a deque with increasing P. When the front already works for end j, record it and drop it: a later end could only give a longer run from that start.

takeaways.md:
- **Shortest subarray with sum ≥ target, negatives allowed:** prefix sums + monotonic deque.
- Discard starts that are dominated (back) or already used (front).
- **Pitfall:** using a sliding window, which needs non-negative values.
